additions.name: AtlasEdge STR001 Stuttgart — operating data centre

status.summary: AtlasEdge's own post published on 2 October 2026 says the company took STR001 in Stuttgart from an almost empty site to customer-ready infrastructure in less than a year and that it runs on 100% renewable electricity with highly efficient cooling. The operator's Stuttgart page lists STR001 at Schickardstraße 19, 71034 Böblingen as 'In operation', in its 14 August 2026 version and already in the 30 July version archived on 2 August 2026. Operation of the STR001 facility is established as of the post's publication day. The 11.2 MW IT capacity and 6,160 m2 white space are final-expansion figures, so no capacity in service is asserted.

locator.precision: Centroid of ALKIS-BW building DEBWL001000uLA5J (Betriebsgebäude, survey quality Katastervermessung), whose location key 08115003-01885-0019 is Schickardstraße 19, Böblingen. The footprint is 3,238.9 m2, about 80 by 80 m, on parcel Dagersheim 3908/21. The point locates the STR001 building, not the 15,921 m2 parcel, the four transformer structures under the same address key, a yard or an entrance.
locator.identity_review: AtlasEdge's Stuttgart page gives STR001's address as Schickardstraße 19, 71034 Böblingen, and its footer links the same address to the Google Maps place 'AtlasEdge Data Centres | Stuttgart' (48.6757596, 8.9669419). The LGL street catalogue (June 2026 edition) resolves Böblingen street key 01885 to Schickardstraße. The ALKIS building with location key 08115003 01885 0019 000 is therefore the addressed building at Schickardstraße 19; it is the only addressed building under that key in the query box. The operator-linked place lies 8.6 m outside this footprint, inside the same parcel and 46.9 m from the centroid. The map viewport centre, 190 m west, is not used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: ALKIS records the footprint at cadastral survey quality but publishes no numeric positional accuracy. The centroid represents a building about 80 m across (42 m from the centroid to the farthest vertex).

additions.name: AtlasEdge LEV002 — new data centre adjacent to LEV001

status.summary: AtlasEdge's Leverkusen page, in its version modified on 14 August 2026, lists LEV002 as 'Under construction'. LEV002 is a data centre that will deliver 4.4 MW of IT capacity and 1,800 m2 of white space for AI and high-density workloads, next to the operating LEV001 at Dornierstraße 10. The Internet Archive copy of 2 August 2026 (the preceding page version, dated 24 April) carries the same label. The operator's 16 April 2026 release says construction began in February 2026 and ready for service is scheduled for Q2 2027. Construction is established as of 14 August 2026. No completion or operation is asserted, and Q2 2027 is a target.

locator.precision: Centroid of the union of the three cadastral parcels with location text 'Dornierstraße 10' (Gemarkung Lützenkirchen, Flur 20, Flurstücke 640, 961 and 962). Together they cover 6,916.0 m2, about 100 by 126 m. The point marks the AtlasEdge Leverkusen campus at LEV001's address. LEV002 is described as adjacent to LEV001 but its plot is not published, so the point does not locate the LEV002 building, its footprint or works.
locator.identity_review: The operator gives LEV001's address as Dornierstraße 10, 51381 Leverkusen, and its 16 April release places LEV002 adjacent to LEV001. NRW ALKIS returns exactly three Leverkusen parcels with location text 'Dornierstraße 10', all in Gemarkung Lützenkirchen Flur 20. The only building addressed 'Dornierstraße 10' is DENW38ALdF00003ABL (1,757 m2, on parcel 962), close to LEV001's stated 1,732 m2 white space. Its centroid lies 22.7 m from the locator. Parcel 961 (3,510 m2) holds only small structures in the cadastre and may be LEV002's plot, but no source says so. Dornierstraße 8 and 11 are separate addressed parcels and are excluded.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The ALKIS service publishes no positional accuracy. The centroid represents a 6,916 m2 parcel group (82.5 m to its farthest vertex). LEV002's position next to LEV001 is not published, so its offset from the point is unknown.

additions.site_name: Polarise AI Factory Amberg (former Wertachtal shortwave transmitter site)
additions.name: Polarise Amberg (Unterallgäu) AI Factory — conversion of the former Wertachtal transmitter building

status.summary: Polarise's release dated Düsseldorf, 9 September 2026 states that its Amberg (Unterallgäu) AI factory in the greater Augsburg area is designed for an initial 65 MW, scalable to 120 MW. It is due to go live in mid-2027 and will be powered largely by on-site solar, wind and battery storage on the former Wertachtal transmitter site. This supports an announced project. No completed acquisition, permit, physical work or operation is established. Mid-2027 is a target, and the release does not say whether 65 MW is IT load.

locator.precision: Centroid of the ATKIS Basis-DLM area 'Ehemalige Kurzwellensendeanlage Wertachtal' (DEBYBDLMbM0001yz), a 3.2 ha ring about 204 m across at the hub of the former antenna field, in the municipality of Amberg, Landkreis Unterallgäu. It marks the former transmitter facility whose transmission building Polarise plans to convert. The largest building in it (LoD2 DEBY_LOD2_2003010, 4,876 m2 footprint, 14.3 m high) lies 35 m away. The point does not locate the adjacent land Polarise plans to acquire, the surrounding solar parks or a construction extent.
locator.identity_review: Polarise's 10 March 2026 release names the site: Polarise will acquire the former Wertachtal shortwave transmission building and the adjacent land and convert them into an AI-ready data centre in the Amberg municipality (Unterallgäu). The 9 September release ties the Amberg (Unterallgäu) AI factory to the former Wertachtal transmitter site. The Bavarian ATKIS Basis-DLM has one area of that name. Its centroid lies inside the ATKIS municipal area 09778111 (Amberg, Landkreis Unterallgäu, not the Upper Palatinate city of Amberg, 09361000), 561 m from the boundary. The official topographic map shows the circular hub with a large central building, surrounded by fenced areas labelled 'Solar'. The LoD2 model does not name buildings, so the transmission building is not separately located.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The Basis-DLM extract states no positional accuracy. The centroid represents a 3.2 ha named area (103 m to its farthest vertex), and the land Polarise will use is not delineated.

additions.site_name: Statesboro Burkhalter Road Data Center Site
additions.name: Statesboro Burkhalter Road proposed data center (4AM Development, RZ 26-07-05)

status.summary: On 18 August 2026 the Statesboro City Council, Georgia, approved 3-2 application RZ 26-07-05, in which 4AM Development, LLC asked to rezone one 26.49-acre parcel at 6539 Burkhalter Road from R-4 to O (Office and Business District) for a proposed data center; the applicant's conceptual plan shows an approximately 230,000 sq ft two-story facility. This dated city record names the project, its developer and its site, which supports announced status. A rezoning is not consent for the data-centre development itself: the city's data-center ordinance still requires a Special Use Permit approved by the council before any building permit, and none had been considered by 20 October 2026, so no permitted status or physical work is asserted.

locator.precision: Centroid of the current Bulloch County parcel polygon PIN 7887-33-7607 (27.05 geodesic acres, about 438 by 580 m) that contains the county 9-1-1 point for 6539 Burkhalter Rd, the 26.49-acre parcel rezoned for the proposed data center. It locates the project parcel, not the conceptual building, a surveyed boundary or the extent of any works.
locator.identity_review: The 18 August 2026 minutes and action agenda name 6539 Burkhalter Road, one parcel of 26.49 acres, as the site of the proposed data center in case RZ 26-07-05. The county address layer has exactly one point for 6539 BURKHALTER RD, and it lies inside current parcel 7887-33-7607 (27.05 acres, 2.1% above the deed-style acreage in the minutes). That parcel and its neighbour 7887-44-4600 (23.76 acres) together reproduce the 50-acre 2022 parcel 108 000001 000 at the same address, so the addressed part of the split is the rezoned tract; the city's zoning layer now codes a 27.99-acre polygon covering 99.99% of it S(O), the Office district approved on 18 August. The minutes print the parcel number as 101 000001 000, which does not occur in the 2022 county table; identity therefore rests on the address, acreage and zoning polygon rather than that number. No geocoder, map viewport, city centre or industrial-park centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The county publishes no positional accuracy for its parcels; the centroid represents a 27-acre parcel about 438 by 580 m, and the planned building position within it is not published.

additions.site_name: QTS Bessemer Data Center Campus (Project Marvel)
additions.name: QTS Bessemer data center campus (Project Marvel) - site preparation

status.summary: QTS's Bessemer, Alabama page, last modified on 20 October 2026, reports that QTS and its partners have started to mobilize equipment onsite, begin clearing and earthwork operations, and start conducting pre-blast surveys for the data center facility QTS is developing in Bessemer. A capture of the same page on 16 October 2026 still said only that equipment 'will begin mobilizing', so the achieved-work wording dates from 16 to 20 October and is observed as of the 20 October modification. This supports site preparation for the campus as a whole; blasting is still to come, and no foundations, building shell, completion or operation is established.

locator.precision: Centroid of the union of the five Jefferson County tax parcels (960.96 geodesic acres in two parts, about 3.2 by 1.6 km) that City of Bessemer Ordinance No. 3698 rezoned, in part, to I-1 for a multi-phased data center. It locates the northern part of the Project Marvel campus (a contiguous 1,555-acre I-1 cluster in the city zoning layer), not a building, the first-phase work area or a surveyed boundary; the 676-acre Rock Mountain Lake Road tract of the campus lies immediately south.
locator.identity_review: QTS's Bessemer page says QTS is developing a data center facility in the Bessemer area and maps its general area with a map centred at (33.34453, -87.03927). That centre lies in parcel 3700352000001000 at 5761 Rock Mountain Lake Rd, part of a 676-acre tract of six Valley Creek Land & Timber LLC parcels that is 99.2% zoned I-1. The City of Bessemer's 20 January 2026 release says an affiliate of the Project Marvel developer agreed to acquire additional land adjacent to the currently zoned parcel, and Ordinance No. 3698 (adopted 21 April 2026) rezones land of AL Bessemer Land, LLC to I-1 for construction and operation of a multi-phased data center: tax parcels 3700270000001000, 3700263000001000, 3700262000001000, 3700261000001000 and 3700264000002000 at 6380, 6042 and 6030 Old Lawsontown Road, 5515 Freeman Ave and 5400 Polara Lane. These parcel numbers and addresses match the city GIS parcel polygons one-to-one. In the city zoning layer they form one contiguous 1,555-acre I-1 cluster with the Rock Mountain Lake Road tract, consistent with the release's 'currently zoned parcel' and the adjacent newly acquired land. The map centre is a viewport centre and is used only for identity, never as the locator. Owner fields (Valley Creek Land & Timber LLC in the June 2026 snapshot) are not used for identity. No geocoder, city centre or industrial-park centroid is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Neither the county nor the city publishes positional accuracy for the parcel layer. The point represents about 961 acres spanning 3.2 by 1.6 km, up to 2.0 km from the centroid, within a 1,555-acre I-1 campus cluster, and the position of the buildings and of the reported site work is not published.

The record moves to the general construction stage as of the release date. The release names no specific stage, so the July 7 building-shell stage is not carried forward and no mechanical, electrical, commissioning or completion stage is inferred. The Phase 1 (December 2026) and Phase 2 (March 2027) completion dates are forecasts.
